insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: Instant addition of 100% Basic Sum Insured on complete or partial utilization of Your existing Policy Sum Insured and cumulative Bonus (if applicable) during the Policy Year.
great.reference: Section B > II. Other Benefits > 1. Restore benefit (Page 11)
great.explanation: The policy replenishes your base Sum Insured by 100% once you use it up within the same policy year. This means you get full extra coverage during the year, improving your financial protection.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as Cumulative Bonus irrespective of any claims
great.reference: Section B > III. Renewal Benefits > 2. Cumulative Bonus (Page 16)
great.explanation: Your Sum Insured increases by 10% at each renewal even if you make claims, so your coverage grows without resetting. This means you keep gaining benefits despite claims.

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
great.reference: Section C > 1(ii) Pre-Existing Diseases: Code - Excl01 (Page 19)
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 24 months from the start of coverage. This means you get earlier coverage for existing conditions compared to longer waiting periods.

good.name: Specific Illness
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.reference: Section C > 1(i) Specified disease/procedure waiting period: Code - Excl02 (Page 16)
good.explanation: Listed surgeries and conditions are excluded for 24 months from policy start. After this period, these treatments are covered as normal.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses... incurred upto 30 days before Hospitalisation.
good.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 2. Pre-Hospitalization Medical expenses (Page 10)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 30 days before hospital admission are covered. This helps pay for tests and treatments before you are hospitalized.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-Hospitalization Medical expenses... incurred upto 60 days after discharge from Hospitalisation.
good.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 3. Post-Hospitalization Medical expenses (Page 10)
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days after hospital discharge are covered. This helps cover follow-up care and medicines after your hospital stay.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: If opted and mentioned on the Policy Schedule that a Co-payment is effective... the insured person shall bear 20% of the eligible claim amount payable under the Policy
bad.reference: Section D > 2. Specific General Terms > 15. Co-Payment (Page 34)
bad.explanation: A 20% co-pay applies only if you choose it and it is shown in your policy schedule. Otherwise, you pay no co-pay, giving you flexibility.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as Food charges (other than patient’s diet provided by hospital), laundry charges, attendant charges, ambulance collar, ambulance equipment, baby food, baby utility charges and other such items. Full list of Non-Medical expenses is attached
bad.reference: Section C > 3. Specific Exclusions > xii (Page 22) and Annexure I List of Non-Medical Expenses (Page 41)
bad.explanation: Many consumables and non-medical items are excluded except in limited cases. This means you may have to pay these costs yourself.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: In-Patient Treatment... includes: • Hospital room rent or boarding
bad.reference: Section B > I. Hospitalisation Covers > 1. In-Patient Treatment (Page 9)
bad.explanation: Room rent is covered but no specific room type or limit is stated, so claims may be reduced if you choose a higher room category. This can cause unexpected deductions.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: If opted and mentioned on the Policy Schedule that a Co-payment is effective...
bad.reference: Section D > 2. Specific General Terms > 15. Co-Payment (Page 34)
bad.explanation: The policy includes a co-pay clause that applies if chosen and shown in the schedule. The presence of any co-pay clause is considered a negative factor as it means you may have to pay part of your claim.

unclear.name: Initial Waiting Period
unclear.quote: All Illnesses and treatments shall be covered subject to the waiting periods specified below:
unclear.explanation: The extract does not explicitly mention an initial waiting period like 30 days. You should verify the full policy wording or schedule for this important detail.
